mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in WORKPLACES mobility over the last four weeks indicates a gradual return to office-based work, which will continue to drive incidental retail and recreation activity during commutes and lunch breaks, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, despite WORKPLACES continuing its upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: A significant week-on-week rebound in TRANSIT mobility, as observed at t-0w, signals a renewed public willingness to travel and engage in out-of-home activities, directly boosting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT increases by more than 3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines in the two weeks following a week where TRANSIT increased by more than 3 points.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent trend of decreasing RESIDENTIAL mobility and increasing WORKPLACES mobility indicates a fundamental shift in daily routines, with more people spending time outside the home, creating more opportunities for retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases over the next 28 days, even if RESIDENTIAL continues to fall and WORKPLACES continues to rise.

mechanism_narrative: A strong rebound in PARKS mobility, especially after a temporary dip, suggests an increase in general outdoor activity and public comfort with out-of-home spaces, which will immediately spill over into increased retail and recreation activity over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS increases by more than 10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not show a positive change in the week following a PARKS increase of more than 10 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility over the last four weeks signifies a sustained trend of people spending less time at home, which inherently translates to more time spent in other categories, including retail and recreation, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days, despite RESIDENTIAL continuing its downward trend.

mechanism_narrative: A divergence where essential mobility (GROCERY_PHARM) is consistently declining while discretionary mobility (RETAIL_REC) shows signs of recovery indicates a shift in consumer confidence and priorities towards non-essential spending, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days, or GROCERY_PHARM reverses its downward trend while RETAIL_REC does not increase.

mechanism_narrative: A strong rebound in PARKS mobility, coupled with a continued decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility, suggests improving weather conditions and a general public desire for out-of-home activities, which will translate into increased RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as people combine outdoor leisure with shopping and dining.
